newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Argentaria to cut debt costs with profits.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Argentaria to cut debt costs with profits.

text.p: Spanish banking group Argentaria plans to use half its 1996 profits to cut liability costs in a bid to boost next year's earnings and sharpen its competitive edge domestically, the chairman said on Thursday.

The group announced late on Wednesday it would channel 42 billion of an estimated 85 billion pesetas ($653.8 million) profit this year into refinancing some 700 billion pesetas of costly fixed-rate long-term debt.
"Our liquidity is excessive. The operation aims to use shareholders' funds more efficiently because our return on equity increases," chairman Francisco Gonzalez told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The move will help the bank cope with pressure on interest margins, amid expectations for continued declines in Spanish interest rates.
"The year 1997 is going to be a very complicated moment for the whole world but less for us because we are a producer of lower costs than the competition," Gonzalez said.
Argentaria also said it would raise its shareholder payout to a gross dividend of 277 pesetas gross per share from 270 pesetas in 1995.
Together with the funds used to reduce liability costs, the dividend rise would leave Argentaria's payout at around 100 percent, leaving it with nothing to allocate to reserves.
The chairman said foreign institutions welcomed the move because it meant better shareholder returns.
"Foreign investors understood very well. It's a purchase of shares. It's a more dynamic way of managing capital," he said.
Analysts said the move would increase the group's profitability in the medium- and long-term but would reduce its liquidity ratios.

"It's good from the strategic point of view because it makes their liabilities cheaper and will give them more room to manoeuvre on the assets side," said Javier Requena, analyst at Benito y Monjardin brokerage.
Shares in Argentaria were at 5300 pesetas by Thursday's close, up 100 from the prior close.
Gonzalez said the bank's strategy is to revitalise its commercial network with an eye to increasing domestic business.
"The bank will make more effort to bolster commercial activity...so that the bank will be stronger in any type of activity," Gonzalez said.
The market had penalised Argentaria more than its competitors for generating less recurrent earnings, he added.
The changes to the bank's financial profile are designed to reduce its reliance on extraordinary profits and boost its basic bank business, he said.
